literal: Prosperity-like ruin and existence-becoming death, to the wise except, is rare.
translation: A ruin that resembles prosperity and a death that becomes an enduring existence are rare to achieve, except for the truly wise.
modern: வளர்ச்சியைப் போன்ற ஒரு வீழ்ச்சியும், நிலைத்து வாழ்தலைத் தரும் ஒரு மரணமும் சிறந்த அறிஞர்களுக்கு அல்லாமல் மற்றவர்களுக்குக் கிடைப்பது அரிது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the unique nature of fame achieved by the truly great. It speaks of a 'ruin' (loss of wealth or life) that acts like 'prosperity' because it brings lasting glory. Similarly, it describes a 'death' that becomes an 'existence' because the person lives on forever in memory. Such paradoxical achievements are impossible except for the wise who know how to live and die for a noble cause.
